before: A mutation in the RTEL1 gene called c.3791G>A (p.R1264H) was found at a carrier frequency of about 1% in the Ashkenazi Orthodox population and about 0.45% in the general Ashkenazi Jewish population, with haplotype evidence pointing to a common founder [1].
This study was designed to recruit people who carry this mutation and to prepare them for possible future trials of gene-directed therapies [2].
This condition primarily affects people of Turkish, Armenian, Arab, and non-Ashkenazi Jewish descent [3].
